(i) qualitative text analysis showed that participants often come across expressions of suicidal thoughts on Instagram; (ii) participants who reported acute suicidal ideation on Instagram were more likely to use negative emotion words and words expressing overall negative affect in interviews; and (iii) activity and language use in Instagram did not predict current suicidality.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether it is possible to identify individuals at high risk for suicide by means of their language use on social media.
the question of whether it is possible to predict suicidality by analysing the language used on social media.
how young people use Instagram to communicate suicidal ideations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Instagram data alone is not sufficient to predict acute suicidiality.
the use of language in Instagram pictures and captions, as well the activity in the Instagram account, does not predict acute suicidity in young people.
the current results are not sufficient to support a statement that language use on Instagram could predict suicidal ideation in the short term.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Instagram is a platform where young people can communicate about their suicidal thoughts and that language use in interviews can help to identify those in need of support.
Instagram is an important communication platform among young people and that it can be used to identify suicidal individuals.
the language used in Instagram pictures does not predict suicidality in young people.
The main takeaway from our work is that
language use in interviews is associated with acute suicidity.
language on social media is a promising tool for identifying suicidal ideation.
the use of social media is an important part of adolescents' lives.
